name: Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC)
funding: Funded directly by Reliance Industries (India largest fossil fuel petrochemical, refining, and telecom conglomerate) under billionaire Mukesh Ambani.

name: Khoj International Artists' Association
funding: Artist-run since 1997. Top supporters: Prince Claus Fund, Goethe-Institut New Delhi and Ford Foundation. Capital circle includes Apeejay Trust, Inlaks India Foundation, Weikfield. Benefactor Sangeeta Jindal.

name: Lalit Kala Akademi
funding: Autonomous body funded by the Union Ministry of Culture, founded in 1954. It runs the National Exhibition, the Triennale-India and seven regional centres.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA)
funding: Government of India. A subordinate office of the Ministry of Culture, founded in 1954, with branches in Mumbai and Bengaluru.

name: Serendipity Arts Festival
funding: Non-profit Serendipity Arts Foundation, founded by Hero Enterprise chair Sunil Kant Munjal. 2025 partners include the Goa government, Hero Insurance Broking, Hero Realty, Campa, Milton and foreign cultural institutes.

name: Selasar Sunaryo Art Space
funding: Founded 1998 by artist Sunaryo with direction and support from the Selasar Sunaryo Foundation.

name: Galeri Nasional Indonesia
funding: State gallery owned by Indonesia's Culture Ministry, a ministry created under President Prabowo; before that it sat under the education and culture ministry. Holds 1,770 artworks.

name: Gudskul (ruangrupa / Serrum / Grafis Huru Hara)
funding: Communal resource pool (lumbung), DOEN Foundation, Arts Collaboratory, and cooperative commercial enterprises. Completely non-corporate collective governance.

name: Jakarta Biennale
funding: Run since 2024 by Majelis Jakarta, an artist-collective network. 2026 partners: Dulux, Artotel's Paviliun Raden Saleh, iForte. Jakarta culture office and Jakpro logos are unlabelled; no budget published.

name: Biennale Jogja
funding: Organised by Yayasan Biennale Yogyakarta, a state-funded foundation created in 2010. The Yogyakarta regional government ran the 2019 edition.
